Subject: QBR: supply & cost synchronization — capacity + unit economics

Team,

As we prep the QBR slides I want a concise alignment on two linked items: (1) near-term capacity/supply posture (Dedicated pool commitments + burst behavior) and (2) expected unit economics (GPU $/token, realized utilization, and the expected delta from batching/caching/quantization changes).

Can each of you own the bullets below and get me numbers and one-slide summaries by COB Thu (2027-08-25)? We're keeping the QBR narrative short — leadership wants clear tradeoffs and where to pull the budget lever if runway looks tight.

- Vivek: baseline GPU spend last 90 days (actual $ and committed $), average GPU utilization by pool (hosted/dedicated/private), and a short list of 'must-try' levers that buy the most cost savings with negligible quality impact. Attach format: sizing-assumptions.xlsx is a starting template.
- Monica: model-level utilization and hot-prefix cache hit rates (sampled), estimates for token reduction from prefix caching + expected latencies when batching window increases to 20–40ms. Include model breakdown CSV.
- Lauren: leadership ask — recommend a buffer policy (commit vs burst) and a single recommendation for the QBR slide (conservative, optimistic, or hybrid).

Attachments: sizing-assumptions.xlsx (skeleton provided). I cc'ed Charlotte from Acme because they care about our buffering plan for Dedicated this quarter.

Thanks — short bullets preferred. I will collate into the QBR one-pager.

—Vanessa
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QBR: supply & cost synchronization — capacity + unit economics

Vanessa —

Thanks. Quick pass with the high-level numbers below. I attached a CSV extract (gpu-run-utilization-q3.csv) with week-by-week utilization and committed vs actual spend.

Summary (last 90 days):
- Actual GPU spend (public & dedicated): $5.4M
- Committed (Reserved) spends: $3.1M (Dedicated contracts) — shortfall covered by burst on hosted pool
- Weighted average GPU utilization: 63% across Dedicated pools; 39% on hosted burst fleet (cost inefficient during peak);
- Median tail latency impact when increasing batching window:
  - 0ms -> 20ms window: +2–5 ms median; 95th percentile +8–15 ms
  - 20ms -> 40ms window: marginal added median latency, but improved batch sizes 12% -> 22% (tokens saved per hour)

Levers with biggest $ impact (order):
1) Increase KV/prefix cache hit via proactive warmers — estimated 9–12% token reduction on typical chat workloads (low quality impact).
2) Fine-grained batch shaping: raise batching threshold to 30ms for background low-latency tiers yields ~18% lower $/token for those requests.
3) Quantization to 4-bit for non-sensitive customer tiers — model-specific; potential 25–40% per-GPU throughput gain but requires validation.

I think the immediate QBR recommendation is a hybrid: modest commit increase for Dedicated (10–15%) + explicit batching policy change for non-critical routes. I'll drop detailed deck bullets.

Regards,
Vivek
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Aug 22, 2027 at 11:40 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Vivek's numbers look right from infra side — I'll add model-level detail.

Attached: model-breakdown.csv — sample of top 12 models by qps with utilization, avg tokens per request, cache hit rate.

Quick findings:
- Top-3 models (chat-general, code-assist, summarizer) account for 64% of token volume.
- Hot-prefix cache hit rates vary: chat-general 28%, code-assist 12%, summarizer 46%.
- Opportunity: raising warm cache targets for chat-general from 30% -> 45% reduces effective token volume ~6.5% and shifts 95th latency down ~10ms in our tests.
- Batching sensitivity: for smaller models (<=3B), batching window 30ms yields +35% throughput with negligible quality delta. For largest models, batching is still beneficial but requires KV-aware batching to avoid cache pollution.

Next steps: I'll run a constrained-sim to project $ delta across three scenarios (baseline, +10% commit, +10% commit + batching policy change) and drop results by Wed EOD.

—Monica

Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turn — good work.

From leadership perspective: we need a single clear recommendation and the downside risk if we don't act. My guidance:
- Recommendation: Hybrid approach (Vivek's suggestion) — increase Dedicated commit by 12% for Q4 to stabilize baseline throughput + implement batching policy change for non-customer-facing low-priority routes. Rationale: immediate $/token improvement while keeping quality exposure limited.
- Downside: If we do nothing, projected spike scenarios (holiday traffic + new partner integrations) could push us into 25–30% higher burst spend for short windows, harming unit economics and predictability.

Please add a one-slide 'what we risk vs what we buy' visual and a single-number ask (incremental $ committed) for the Ops/Finance slide. Include the Drive link where we keep the QBR slides.

—Lauren
